repo_notes.content: Repository identity: famousspotsapp-ship-it/godot is a fork of upstream godotengine/godot tracking the `master` branch at engine version 4.7-beta (see version.py: major=4, minor=7, patch=0, status="beta"). The only fork-specific code is the `steel_streets/` directory, a standalone GDScript demo game project. Every other directory (core/, servers/, scene/, editor/, main/, platform/, drivers/, modules/, thirdparty/, tests/, doc/, misc/) is upstream Godot engine code. Never attribute engine C++ code to Steel Streets, and never describe Steel Streets as part of the engine build: SCons does not compile or reference steel_streets/.

Architecture layering to use consistently across pages: `core/` (Object/ClassDB, Variant, math, io, os, config, input) is the foundation and must not depend on other layers. `servers/` (rendering, physics_2d, physics_3d, navigation_2d, navigation_3d, audio, text, display, xr, camera, movie_writer, debugger) builds on core. `scene/` (main, 2d, 3d, gui, animation, resources, theme) builds on core and servers. `editor/` builds on everything and is only compiled when TOOLS_ENABLED (target=editor). `main/main.cpp` wires the layers together during startup. `platform/<name>/` (android, ios, linuxbsd, macos, visionos, web, windows) implements OS and DisplayServer; `drivers/` holds shared backends (vulkan, d3d12, metal, gles3, unix, windows, apple, apple_embedded, sdl, accesskit, audio drivers). `modules/` are optional components registered via register_types.cpp and config.py (gdscript, mono, openxr, webxr, text_server_adv, navigation, etc.).

Team build/test workflow (Linux dev VM): build with `scons tests=yes target=editor dev_build=yes -j$(nproc)`; linking needs ~8 GB RAM (swap configured). The resulting binary is `bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64`. Run unit tests headless with `./bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 --headless --test`, and filter with `--test-case="*AnimationPlayer*"`. Lint via `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` using .pre-commit-config.yaml (clang-format, clang-tidy, ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy, codespell, make-rst, doc-status, validate-xml, validate-includes, copyright-headers, header-guards, file-format, dotnet-format, eslint, svgo). Include these exact commands on the Building, Test Suite and Development Workflow pages.

Citation accuracy rules: only cite files that actually implement the behavior being described on a page. For Steel Streets, cite files under steel_streets/ (project.godot, scripts/*.gd, scenes/*.tscn, tools/gen_assets.py, README.md), not modules/gdscript internals. In architecture diagrams, map Node to scene/main/node.h, SceneTree to scene/main/scene_tree.h, Control to scene/gui/control.h, and EditorNode to editor/editor_node.h. Keep thirdparty library details (e.g. Embree, thirdparty/README.md) on the Modules/Thirdparty page, not on CI or workflow pages.

pages.title: Steel Streets Demo Game
pages.purpose: Document the fork-specific steel_streets/ Godot project: project configuration, scene flow, GDScript architecture, gameplay systems, and the procedural asset generation pipeline in tools/gen_assets.py. This is team-owned code and should be documented in concrete detail.

page_notes.content: Facts from project.godot: config_version=5, features "4.3" + "GL Compatibility" (renderer gl_compatibility on desktop and mobile), main scene res://scenes/title_screen.tscn, 160x144 viewport scaled to a 640x576 window with stretch mode viewport / aspect keep, nearest texture filter, 2D pixel snapping. Autoload: GameManager = res://scripts/game_manager.gd. Input actions: move_left, move_right, jump, attack, climb_up, climb_down, start (keyboard + gamepad). 2D physics layer names: 1 world, 2 player, 3 player_hitbox, 4 enemy, 5 enemy_hitbox, 6 ladder, 7 pickup, 8 hazard. Run with `godot --path steel_streets` using a built or downloaded Godot 4.3+ binary.

Scene flow: title_screen -> splash_screen (auto-advances after 2.5 s or on input) -> level_1 -> game_over or victory -> title. All transitions go through GameManager.goto_title/goto_splash/goto_level/goto_game_over/goto_victory, which call SceneTree.change_scene_to_file. GameManager also owns run state (lives=3, hp=5, score) and emits score_changed, lives_changed, hp_changed; take_life() returns false when lives run out.

Scripts (steel_streets/scripts/): player.gd (CharacterBody2D; walk/jump/melee attack/ladder climb, knockback and 1.2 s invincibility), enemy_base.gd (CharacterBody2D base with hp, contact damage, score_value, hurtbox/hitbox handling, death), foot_soldier.gd (patrol + chase with ledge detection), shuriken_thrower.gd (paces and fires projectile.tscn every 1.6 s within sight range), boss.gd (state machine PAUSE -> WINDUP -> CHARGE -> RECOVER, emits boss_hp_changed and boss_defeated), projectile.gd, question_block.gd (score + small heal), hud.gd (CanvasLayer hearts/score/lives and boss bar via attach_boss), level_1.gd, anim_util.gd (builds SpriteFrames from horizontal sprite strips via AtlasTexture), and title/splash/game_over/victory screen scripts. Enemies subclass enemy_base.gd via path-based `extends "res://scripts/enemy_base.gd"`, not class_name.

level_1.gd builds the level procedurally at runtime: a 100x9 grid of 16 px tiles, a TileSet built in code from assets/sprites/tiles/tileset.png, background and foreground painted on a TileMap node (the legacy TileMap class, not TileMapLayer), then ladders, spikes, pickups, foot soldiers, shuriken throwers, the boss (column 92) and the HUD are instanced from constant tables (PLATFORMS, LADDERS, SPIKES, PICKUPS, FOOT_SOLDIERS, SHURIKEN_THROWERS, BOSS_POS). Defeating the boss waits 1.5 s then calls GameManager.goto_victory().

Asset pipeline: tools/gen_assets.py (Python 3 + Pillow + stdlib wave/struct) procedurally generates every PNG sprite sheet (player, enemies, projectiles, tiles, items, UI and bitmap text) from ASCII pixel rows restricted to the 4-color Game Boy palette #e0f8d0 / #88c070 / #346856 / #081820, and every chiptune WAV (square tones, slides, noise bursts, BGM loop). It does NOT compress textures or preprocess external raw art. Regenerate with `python3 steel_streets/tools/gen_assets.py` after `pip install Pillow`; Godot re-imports the outputs (.import files are committed).
